comparison: Both evaluate the core methodological approach (C2, C3, C27-29) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on technical validation of the PC-corr method and network analysis, while peer reviewers emphasize the approach as 'accessible, sound and well described' and 'a new type of approach for mechanobiology.' Strong agreement on methodological soundness.

Both address methodological contributions (C68, C70-73) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval evaluates hypothesis-free nature and cross-system integration with some speculation about future applications. Peer reviewers affirm this provides 'a new type of approach' without questioning the methodological claims. Agreement on methodological innovation.

Both evaluate expression pattern findings (C39-42) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes non-monotonic relationships are documented but interpretation is speculative. Peer reviewers accept validation as 'thorough' and 'well-validated' without specific critique of these claims. Agreement on data quality, though OpenEval more cautious about interpretation.

Both evaluate in silico validation (C43-47) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of AUC-ROC values and negative controls. Peer reviewers affirm validation is 'thorough' and 'well-validated using in silico and experimental approaches.' Strong agreement on validation quality.

Both evaluate JVT statistical validation (C48, C50) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the novel and conservative nature of JVT method. Peer reviewers include these in their general affirmation that results are 'thoroughly tested.' Agreement on statistical rigor.

Both evaluate CAV1 knockdown experiments (C56-57) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details multiple RNAi constructs and orthogonal validation across three measurement techniques. Peer reviewers explicitly state authors 'show convincingly' that CAV1 affects cell mechanics. Strong agreement on experimental validation.

Both evaluate CAV1 overexpression (C58-59) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes interpretation about basal CAV1 responsiveness is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers include this in their affirmation that 'changing its expression level affects cell mechanics.' Agreement on core findings with OpenEval noting interpretive caution.

Both evaluate MCF10A-ER-Src gain/loss-of-function analysis (C62-66) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes bidirectional perturbations provide strong causal evidence. Peer reviewers describe this as 'convincing' evidence without specific concerns. Strong agreement on causal validation.

Both evaluate CAV1 knockout data (C108) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes this provides orthogonal genetic evidence. Peer reviewers include this in their general affirmation of 'convincing' experimental validation. Agreement on supporting evidence quality.

Both evaluate baseline characterization (C51-52) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details western blot and mechanical measurements across methods. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the 'convincing' CAV1 validation. Agreement on baseline data quality.

Both evaluate mechanical characterization across five systems (C19, C20, C22, C24, C26) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval details statistical analysis and replication. Peer reviewers accept these as 'thoroughly tested' foundational measurements. Agreement on data quality and rigor.

Both evaluate RT-DC methodology (C13-15) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes established method with proper citations. Peer reviewers note 'different types of mechanical characterisations' without concerns. Agreement on methodological soundness.

Both evaluate frequency-dependent mechanical variation (C53-55) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes alignment with literature. Peer reviewers accept multiple measurement approaches as part of authors' 'great effort.' Agreement on technical rigor.

Both address GO analysis results (C77-79) but with different evaluations. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with reasonable interpretation that lack of mechanics terms indicates novel associations. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether findings represent central mechanisms or peripheral effects. Disagreement on biological significance interpretation.

Both evaluate novelty claim (C91) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes some uncertainty about comprehensive literature coverage. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as 'a new type of approach for mechanobiology.' Agreement on novelty with OpenEval slightly more cautious.

Both evaluate literature comparisons (C92-95) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes overlaps with prior studies provide external validation. Peer reviewers affirm novelty of the approach without questioning these comparisons. Agreement on contextual validity.

Both evaluate literature-based gene characterizations (C30-38) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these establish biological plausibility but are not novel findings. Peer reviewers accept without challenge as background context. Agreement that literature synthesis is accurate.

Both evaluate mechanotransduction pathway connections (C80-90) as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes YAP signaling connections with proper citations but notes lack of experimental validation. Peer reviewers accept without disputing individual characterizations. Agreement on literature-based contextualization.

Both address future applications (C103, C105-107) but with different evaluations. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting claims about AI algorithms and therapeutic applications are speculative. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, viewing these as reasonable motivations for future work. Disagreement on whether speculative future directions warrant support.

Both address future applications (C69) with different emphasis. OpenEval rates overall methodological contribution as SUPPORTED but notes future application claims are speculative. Peer reviewers view forward-looking statements as reasonable implications. Partial agreement with different perspectives on speculation.
